_: Le perron du 129 Frank-Robinson. Margaret is Tom's mother: she is at home, never on this porch (ledger s.0); Abraham takes her place in the roster (Tom approved Abraham in the gang, 29 Sept; his porch lines are PROPOSAL). `need` is a space-separated list of conditions; every one has to hold. Tokens: done:<id>, !done:<id>, couch, !couch, car:<id>, radio:on, radio:off, here:<key> (that person is on the lawn tonight), and <fact><op><n> over races/jobs/money/damage/nights/best. More conditions = more specific = said first. `gift` pays out once ever. Zahra's about-sayyad lines come from zahra.json and are folded in with need 'here:sayyad'. src/game/hangout.js carries a trimmed copy of this file as its fallback.
day: L'entrée est vide. La Buick de la mère de Mike est là, pas Mike.
Y a personne. Le monde arrive quand le soleil descend.
Le perron est vide. C'est un perron de soir, ça.

greet.line: Kill the engine. My mom's asleep at ten.
Perfect timing. I was explaining something important. Hear me out.
FINALLY. Twenty minutes of talking about nothing.
New PowerBook. The keyboard lights up. It LIGHTS UP, Tom.
Sit. There's room on the steps.
Hey man. I brought my guitar. Nobody asked.
Sayyad says your licence isn't real. I don't believe him. But he said it.
I'm in by ten. Not by choice.

catch.line: ...so the guy tells me the engine's fine. FINE. Listen. Listen to me for two seconds.
There's one way to back into the driveway without hitting the bin. One. I'll show you with my hands.
Look at it. LOOK AT IT. Three weeks up there. That's engineering.
My mom saw it yesterday. Said nothing. NOTHING. That's the best part.
People slow down in front of the house to see it. People. Slow down. For US.
I have a plan for the couch. A real plan. I just need your truck.
It came down. No idea how. Bring the truck, we lift it back up.
You beat his Civic?! Wait. Wait wait wait. Start from the beginning.
A canoe. Bondo. To the island. I told three people and nobody believes me.
You came in a BUS. A school bus. In MY driveway. Honestly.
That's... that's a golf cart. Ok. OK! Fine, ok. Explain.
What happened to the car?! No. Don't tell me. Tell me. Tell me everything.
You did more this summer than I've done in my whole life, and I'm a year older than you.
No no no, listen. Hear me out. The mechanic charges double if you wait. DOUBLE. Watch my hand.
...and that's when Zahra said I had it backwards. She was right. Listen anyway.
Wait wait wait. Both of you. Listen to me at the same time. This is important.
The Tour des Maringouins isn't a race, it's a nerve test. Watch my hands: THIS is the turn.
What is that? No. No no no. Take that off and put my CD in.
There's no music. Why is there no music? Turn on the radio, man.
I burned a mix last night. Blink, 50 Cent, and one Jean Leloup song for my mom.
My Civic would eat you alive. We say it once and we move on.
I let you win that night. To be nice. Ask Adam.
Three doughnuts in front of my house and I heard nothing. My mom still talks about it.
The couch was my idea. Mike will say it was his. It was my idea.
You came in MY Civic. ...go on. I'm fine. Keep talking.
You're broke, eh? It's all over your face, my man.
Where did you get that money? No. Forget it. I don't want to know.
Six checkpoints, one clock. The town is yours. Officially.
Three races. Nobody in Aylmer wants to race you anymore. That includes me.
Sit for two minutes. Leaving at ten or ten fifteen changes nothing.
Same party in Deschênes every Friday and they think we don't know.
Your truck, man. What happened to your truck?
Nachos at five in the morning. I'd go again.
You work a lot for a summer. There won't be another one like this, you know.
There's a couch in the tree. I'm going to pretend I didn't see it.
You race on streets where people live. One day you'll get that.
You come every night now. That's fine. That's a summer.
Your mom gave me juice. Twice. I think she likes me. Or she's watching me.
Here. Ten bucks. No, take it. Pay me back in September.
...yeah.
I walked from Mayo. ...no. I have the Sunfire. Just checking if you listen.
My Sunfire is faster than your car. That's math.
You beat me. Once. On one street. On a Tuesday. In July.
That's my car.
There's a couch in the tree.
You drove up to Chelsea. For nothing. ...respect.
Your car looks like my life.
Hull. You went to Hull. They have a museum, apparently. I'm not going.
You all say the same things every night. I counted. There are eleven.
The couch will fall. Not tonight. But it will fall, and someone will be under it.
How many races did you win? Two? Sayyad told my mom five. Wrong.
You have money and you still drive the Ranger. Explain that to me.
Right fender. You hit it backing up. I saw the paint on the post.
You stole a golf cart. I'm telling nobody. It's going to cost you, though.
Thirty-one seconds. I timed you. Sayyad said forty and he's lying.
You're here more than I am, and I live three streets over.
You've done every job in town. What's left, besides us?
The island is 1.2 km out. I measured it on the geography map. You're all insane.
Mike has been explaining the same thing since Tuesday. Nobody told him we got it.
Take it to the mechanic before your mom sees it. He won't say anything. He never does.
The neighbour's cat followed me here. It's staying. It's my cat now.
Touch my bag and you'll meet my nails.
Zahra, your brother says it's time. ...I'm just passing it on.
Don't listen to her. She thinks she's right. ...she's usually right.

pitch.line: My mom's bins are already on the street. Down to Smiley and back. Timed.
I put the bins out. Slalom to Smiley, back into the driveway. Ten bucks.
I have my dad's watch. The clock starts when you move. Don't cheat.
Bins are out. Go to Smiley. Come back. That's it.

win.line: YEAH! DID YOU SEE THAT? Did anyone see that?
The third bin. How did you do the third bin? Show me with your hands.
That's a good time. I won't say it too loud, they'll want to go again.
Nice work. Now pick up the bins, it's garbage day tomorrow.

lose.line: Let me try. LET ME TRY.
You missed two gates and broke a bin. I wrote it all down.
It's fine. It's FINE. The bin was in a dumb spot. That's on me.

job.line: I've got something for you. Get in, I'll explain on the way.
There's a thing to do tonight. Clean money.
There's a job. I'd go, but I won't.
AH! I forgot. I FORGOT. Wait. Hear me out.
I read the ad. Nobody else did. Go before they do.

leave.line: Come back tomorrow! I'll have finished explaining.
Honk when you drive by. Every time.
Drive slow on the street. There are kids.
Bye. No stupid stuff before tomorrow.
